title: India bond traders seen leaning bearish in early trade with eyes on fresh supply - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Indian government bonds are set to start the session with a bias ​towardsdeclining on Friday, as markets await fresh supply of debt ‌at a time when slower foreign buying is ​testingdomestic investor appetite.

The benchmark Indian 6.94 per cent ⁠2036 bond yield is expected to move in the range of 6.80 per cent-6.84 per cent, according to a trader at a private-sector bank, after ‌closing at 6.8132 per cent on Thursday. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

New Delhi is due to ‌raise 340 billion rupees ($3.55 billion) through sale of ‌the ⁠benchmark note, which will take the outstanding value ⁠of this paper to 1.36 trillion rupees.

"We could see some selling initially with traders making space in their portfolios to absorb ​the new supply, but ‌cutoffs would determine whether we test 6.85 per cent before the central bank decision," the trader said.

The Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy decision is due on Wednesday. It ‌is widely expected to keep its key ​interest rate unchanged, according to a Reuters poll of economists.

The decision comes after the Federal ⁠Reserve held interest rates on Wednesday, though Chair Kevin Warsh said the central bank would remain focused on bringing ‌inflation down, leaving markets uncertain over the policy outlook.

"Watching Kevin Warsh was disappointing as he tried to appear hawkish by saying that 2 per cent inflation target is sacrosanct, but could not explain the reason for not taking any action like hiking rates," said Sandeep Bagla, ‌CEO, TRUST Mutual Fund.

Meanwhile, the benchmark Brent crude contract traded ​around $88 per barrel, as market participants digested proposed plans for a Saudi Arabia-led maritime coalition ⁠to boost defense cooperation around the Red Sea.

India's overnight ⁠index swap rates are expected to consolidate, after witnessing a sharp spike through the month.

The one-year ‌rate ended at 5.92 per cent, while the two-year rate closed at 6.12 per cent on Thursday. The liquid five-year rate ​settled at 6.42 per cent.
